extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A visual question answering dataset containing questions that require reading and reasoning about text in images. It contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images, with each question-image pair having 10 ground truth answers provided by humans.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The TextVQA dataset was newly created by collecting questions from sighted humans on selected Open Images photos from categories likely to contain text, and each question-image pair was annotated with 10 human-provided ground truth answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the Open Images dataset, specifically from categories that tend to contain text such as billboard, traffic sign, and whiteboard.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were asked by sighted humans on images, and each question-image pair received 10 ground-truth answers provided by humans.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators asking questions were sighted humans.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that standard VQA datasets contain linguistic priors that models can exploit without proper visual grounding, and that existing datasets underrepresent text-reading questions because they were not collected in settings resembling visually impaired users' real-world needs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is built from Open Images categories likely to contain text, which may limit generalization. The paper also notes that some questions require combining multiple OCR tokens, which the proposed approach cannot handle; 8.9% of TextVQA questions fall into this case and are left for future work.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is motivated by assistive applications for visually impaired users, since reading-related questions are common in that setting and current VQA models perform poorly on them.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Visual disability status of the target user population is discussed as a human attribute in the motivation, and the dataset questions are asked by sighted humans rather than visually impaired users.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced to facilitate research progress and benchmarking for VQA models that must read and reason about text in images; it is used to train and evaluate such models.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were collected on Open Images images from categories likely to contain text, and image/question inputs were converted into model-ready representations using pretrained word embeddings for question words and OCR tokens, recurrent encoding for questions, and extracted visual features from pooled ResNet-152 grid features and Faster-RCNN region features.
